prevailing-wage-fringe.formula: package = base + fringe; cash_burden = fringe x burden%; plan_saves_per_hr = fringe x burden% (fringe funded through a bona-fide plan is not taxable wages).
prevailing-wage-fringe.edition: The prevailing-wage total package (base wage plus fringe) and the payroll-burden savings of paying fringe through a bona-fide plan versus as cash, by name.
prevailing-wage-fringe.freeAccess: Prevailing-wage determinations are published free at sam.gov (Davis-Bacon) and state DOL sites; the burden rate is user-supplied.
prevailing-wage-fringe.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
prevailing-wage-fringe.editionNote: A prevailing-wage determination sets a total package = a base hourly wage plus an hourly fringe amount. Paying the fringe as extra cash makes it taxable wages, so the employer owes payroll burden (FICA, and often workers-comp and other wage-based costs) on it; funding the same fringe through a bona-fide benefit plan (health, pension, training) satisfies the obligation without adding taxable wages, saving fringe x the wage-based burden per hour. At just FICA (7.65%) a $15 fringe saves about $1.15/hr; at a fuller 15% burden it saves about $2.25/hr, real money across a crew and a job. The applicable wage determination and whether the plan qualifies as bona-fide under Davis-Bacon / the state statute govern.

assumptions.name: Package
assumptions.value: total package = base wage + hourly fringe

assumptions.name: Bona-fide plan
assumptions.value: fringe paid into a bona fide plan counts toward the prevailing wage, and employer contributions to qualified retirement and health plans are generally not FICA wages; cash fringe is taxable wages

assumptions.name: Unfunded plans
assumptions.value: a self-funded (unfunded) plan's cost is credited only after the contractor requests and receives the Secretary's approval (added 2023-10-23)

assumptions.name: Determination governs
assumptions.value: the wage determination and the plan's bona-fide status govern

fan-motor-bhp.formula: AHP = CFM * TSP / 6356; BHP = AHP / eta_fan; motor HP = BHP / eta_drive, rounded up to the next standard NEMA MG 1 size (none is listed above 300 hp).
fan-motor-bhp.edition: AMCA / ASHRAE fan-power relation BHP = (CFM * SP) / (6356 * eta) (public); standard motor HP sizes per NEMA MG 1, by name.
fan-motor-bhp.freeAccess: Free principles in published HVAC texts; the 6356 constant is a pure unit derivation.
fan-motor-bhp.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
fan-motor-bhp.editionNote: Single-relation; TSP must be total static (external + internal) and efficiency at the duty point. Fan curve and motor data govern.

assumptions.name: Total static pressure
assumptions.value: external + internal static, not just external

termination-temp-ampacity.formula: termination_ampacity = (termination_rating == 75 ? amp_75c : amp_60c); nec_default_column = over_100a ? 75 : 60 (reported, flags a 60 C termination above 100 A); derated_90c = amp_90c x derate_factor; governing = min(termination_ampacity, derated_90c).
termination-temp-ampacity.edition: NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). 110.14(C) (temperature limitations of terminations) with Table 310.16.
termination-temp-ampacity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
termination-temp-ampacity.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: 90 C for derating only
assumptions.value: the 90 C column may be used only for the ambient and fill derating math, not for the final termination current

assumptions.name: Termination column by size
assumptions.value: at or below 100 A use 60 C unless all terminations and conductors are listed 75 C; above 100 A use 75 C

battery-runtime.formula: Runtime = (battery_Wh × inverter_efficiency × depth_of_discharge) / load_W. Coulombic adjustments via Peukert exponent for lead-acid only.
battery-runtime.edition: Battery-chemistry physical facts; manufacturer datasheets by name.
battery-runtime.freeAccess: Datasheets free on each manufacturer site.
battery-runtime.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.

assumptions.name: Inverter efficiency
assumptions.value: 100% (DC / ideal) unless user supplies; enter ~90% for an AC load through an inverter

assumptions.name: DoD limit
assumptions.value: user-supplied depth of discharge (default 100%); typical practice is 80% LFP / 50% lead-acid

loto-steps.formula: (reference page; no compute) Standard 9-step lockout / tagout sequence (notify, identify, shut down, isolate, lock, release stored energy, verify, service, reverse) as required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 (control of hazardous energy).
loto-steps.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
loto-steps.editionNote: Single-edition (29 CFR 1910.147 stable since 1989; refreshed if OSHA updates).

brake-pad-life.formula: KE = 0.5 × m × v² per stop (J). Rotor temperature rise per stop ΔT = 0.20 × KE / (mass_rotor × 460 J/kg-K), taking one rotor as absorbing about a fifth of the stop's energy. Pad wear per stop = KE (kJ) × a per-kJ wear rate by pad chemistry; life = pad thickness / wear per stop, split front/rear by the brake bias.
brake-pad-life.edition: Classical kinetic-energy theorem; SAE J661 friction test, SAE J2522 (brake performance) by name; manufacturer pad-chemistry technical bulletins (Akebono, EBC, Hawk, StopTech).
brake-pad-life.freeAccess: SAE licensed; physical-fact derivations free in mechanics texts.
brake-pad-life.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

assumptions.name: Specific heat (cast-iron rotor)
assumptions.value: 460 J/kg-K (0.11 BTU/lb-°F); one rotor takes about 20% of the stop energy

assumptions.name: Wear rates
assumptions.value: organic 2.0e-5, semi-metallic 1.2e-5, ceramic 0.9e-5 mm per kJ (illustrative defaults; a shop-measured rate overrides)
assumptions.source: planning defaults, not a published benchmark

codon-table.formula: Standard genetic-code lookup: each in-frame triplet of RNA bases (A / C / G / U) maps to an amino acid or a STOP codon. DNA sequences are translated by replacing T with U before lookup.
codon-table.edition: Standard genetic code (universal). IUPAC-IUB amino-acid one- and three-letter codes.
codon-table.freeAccess: Public domain reference. Available in every introductory molecular-biology textbook and at ncbi.nlm.nih.gov.
codon-table.governance: Estimate only. Readability formulas and similar metrics are derived from a representative population and have known edge-case noise. The classroom teacher governs final text selection, grade placement, and assessment decisions.
codon-table.editionNote: Mitochondrial and certain bacterial / protozoan genetic codes differ at specific codons (e.g., UGA codes for Trp in vertebrate mitochondria, not STOP) and are NOT covered by this tile. Reading frame starts at position 1 of the entered sequence; the tile does not search for an internal start codon.

assumptions.name: Code
assumptions.value: standard / universal genetic code

assumptions.name: Reading frame
assumptions.value: starts at position 1 of the input
assumptions.source: convention; for ORF finding use a dedicated tool

assumptions.name: Trailing partial codon
assumptions.value: 1 or 2 trailing bases are ignored (no partial codon translated)

horizontal-sightline-offset.formula: M = R (1 - cos(28.65 S / R)) [half-angle in degrees]; inverse S = (R/28.65) arccos(1 - M/R); R to the inside-lane centerline.
horizontal-sightline-offset.edition: The AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (the Green Book) horizontal sightline offset (middle ordinate), by name.
horizontal-sightline-offset.freeAccess: The AASHTO middle-ordinate relation is published in the Green Book. AHJ, state DOT design manual, and the licensed civil engineer of record govern.
horizontal-sightline-offset.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
horizontal-sightline-offset.editionNote: The AASHTO Green Book middle-ordinate M = R (1 - cos(28.65 S / R)) with R to the inside-lane centerline (the vehicle's path), the inverse S = (R/28.65) arccos(1 - M/R), and that the offset is measured from the sightline to the sight obstruction. This returns the horizontal sightline offset (clear-zone width) for the entered sight distance and radius: it uses R to the vehicle's path (inside-lane centerline, not the curve centerline), assumes the sight obstruction is continuous along the curve, and does not account for the driver-to-obstruction geometry at the curve ends or a variable offset. A design aid, not a substitute for a licensed civil engineer's design.

assumptions.name: Middle-ordinate model
assumptions.value: M = R (1 - cos(28.65 S / R)), the 28.65 = 90/pi putting the half-angle in degrees

assumptions.name: Radius basis
assumptions.value: R is to the inside-lane centerline (the vehicle's path), not the curve centerline

assumptions.name: Continuous obstruction
assumptions.value: assumes the sight obstruction runs continuously along the curve; no end geometry

vertical-curve.formula: Equal-tangent parabola from the BVC: elev(x) = bvc_elev + (g1/100)*x + ((g2-g1)/100)/(2L)*x^2, x in ft from BVC. Turning point at x = -g1*L/(g2-g1) when it lies in [0, L].
vertical-curve.edition: Equal-tangent parabolic vertical-curve elevations and the high/low-point location per the AASHTO Green Book vertical-alignment relations and FM 5-233, by name; first-principles.
vertical-curve.freeAccess: FM 5-233 is public-domain US Government work, free at US Army publication archives. The design of record governs.
vertical-curve.governance: Estimate. Engineer of record governs the design and acceptance. Verify against the project structural drawings and the manufacturer's published capacity / chart.
vertical-curve.editionNote: Single-edition (first-principles parabolic geometry). Equal grades (g1 = g2) report a straight grade rather than dividing by zero.

assumptions.name: Symmetric curve
assumptions.value: equal-tangent (symmetric) parabola; unequal-tangent curves out of scope

sheathing-takeoff.formula: sheets = ceil(area_sf x (1 + waste_pct/100) / sheet_sf); nails = sheets x nails_per_sheet.
sheathing-takeoff.edition: Sheathing panel / nail takeoff identity by name (sheets from area over panel area; nails from the schedule); first-principles count arithmetic.
sheathing-takeoff.freeAccess: The takeoff is public quantity arithmetic; the nailing schedule comes from the plans and the code (entered here, not reproduced).
sheathing-takeoff.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
sheathing-takeoff.editionNote: The nails-per-sheet comes from the nailing schedule the carpenter reads off the plans - a 6-in edge / 12-in field pattern is about 60 nails on a 4x8, a 4-in / 6-in shear panel far more (the value is entered, not reproduced from a code table). Distinct from the plywood-span rating and the residential-framing lumber rollup.

assumptions.name: Panel area
assumptions.value: 32 sf for a 4x8 sheet; the sheet size governs

assumptions.name: Nails per sheet
assumptions.value: from the nailing schedule on the plans (~60 for a 6/12 field pattern, ~100+ for a shear panel)

round-to-rect-duct.formula: ASHRAE equal-friction equivalent diameter D_e = 1.30*(a*b)^0.625/(a+b)^0.250. Round-to-rect solves the unknown side for a target D_e; aspect ratio = long side / short side.
round-to-rect-duct.edition: The ASHRAE equal-friction circular equivalent of a rectangular duct, D_e = 1.30*(a*b)^0.625/(a+b)^0.250, per ASHRAE Fundamentals (duct design) and SMACNA, by name; first-principles.
round-to-rect-duct.freeAccess: First-principles equal-friction equivalence (not equal-velocity). The fabrication drawing governs.
round-to-rect-duct.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
round-to-rect-duct.editionNote: ASHRAE Fundamentals / SMACNA. An equal-friction equivalence, noted inline. An aspect ratio above 4:1 fires the sheet-metal-practical-limit flag. Pairs with duct-sizing.

assumptions.name: Equivalence basis
assumptions.value: equal friction, not equal velocity

decimal-to-fraction.formula: ticks = round(value * den); whole = floor(ticks/den); fraction = (ticks - whole*den)/den reduced by GCD; feet = floor(whole/12); error = rounded - exact.
decimal-to-fraction.edition: Decimal-to-fraction tape-measure math - nearest 1/N rounding, GCD reduction, and feet-inch decomposition; first-principles arithmetic, public domain.
decimal-to-fraction.freeAccess: Pure arithmetic, public; binary (power-of-two) denominators are the tape-measure / machinist-scale standard.
decimal-to-fraction.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
decimal-to-fraction.editionNote: First-principles arithmetic; the error reported is the rounded value minus the exact decimal, so the user can see the rounding loss.

assumptions.name: Binary denominators
assumptions.value: rounds to a power-of-two tape-measure fraction (2/4/8/16/32/64)

wireless-fspl.formula: FSPL(dB) = 32.44 + 20 log10(d_km) + 20 log10(f_MHz); received power Pr = Pt + Gt + Gr - FSPL (all dB). The 32.44 constant is for distance in km and frequency in MHz.
wireless-fspl.edition: The Friis transmission equation / free-space path loss, per ITU-R P.525, by name; first-principles RF.
wireless-fspl.freeAccess: The Friis / FSPL relation is public first-principles physics and ITU-R P.525 is a free ITU download; the distance, frequency, power, and antenna gains are the user's link inputs.
wireless-fspl.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
wireless-fspl.editionNote: The free-space path loss of a line-of-sight radio link and the resulting received signal, the wireless sibling of the fiber and coax loss budgets. FSPL(dB) = 32.44 + 20 log10(d_km) + 20 log10(f_MHz), so the loss climbs 6 dB every time distance or frequency doubles - a 2.4 GHz link over 1 km loses 100.0 dB, and at 5.8 GHz about 107.7 dB. The received power is Pr = Pt + Gt + Gr - FSPL, so a 20 dBm radio with 12 dBi antennas each end over that 1 km 2.4 GHz path delivers -56 dBm. This is IDEAL free space only: it excludes cable and connector loss, atmospheric and rain attenuation, obstruction and Fresnel-zone diffraction, multipath, and terrain, and a real link carries a fade margin over this - compare the received power to the receiver sensitivity separately. A planning estimate; the path survey and radio spec govern.

assumptions.name: Free-space path loss
assumptions.value: FSPL = 32.44 + 20 log10(d_km) + 20 log10(f_MHz)

assumptions.name: Received power
assumptions.value: Pr = Pt + Gt + Gr - FSPL (dB); ideal free space, no cable/atmospheric/obstruction loss

counterweight-arbor-load.formula: required = (batten_weight + attached_load) x purchase_ratio (1 single, 2 double); out_of_weight = required - existing; bricks = ceil(|out_of_weight| / brick_weight).
counterweight-arbor-load.edition: Theatrical counterweight rigging (single / double purchase), by name.
counterweight-arbor-load.freeAccess: Standard stagecraft counterweight-balance relation; the venue rigging inspection and the AHJ govern.
counterweight-arbor-load.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
counterweight-arbor-load.editionNote: A double-purchase system needs two pounds of counterweight per pound on the batten (and the arbor travels half as far), so reversing the ratio lets the pipe run away; the arbor is loaded only when the batten is at the loading rail (an out-of-weight batten is the classic fly-rail hazard); arbor capacity is finite. A balancing aid, not a rigging inspection.

assumptions.name: Purchase ratio
assumptions.value: 1:1 single, 2:1 double (double travels half the distance, needs twice the counterweight)

key-cut-macs-check.formula: for every adjacent pair, the absolute difference between cut depths must not exceed the manufacturer MACS value; the shortfall on a failing pair is that difference less MACS.
key-cut-macs-check.edition: The maximum adjacent cut specification rule by name, with the lock manufacturer's cut specification named as governing the value, the depth increment, the allowable range, root spacing, and cut angle.
key-cut-macs-check.freeAccess: Absolute differences on a bitting the user enters, against a value from the manufacturer; no cut specification is reproduced.
key-cut-macs-check.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
key-cut-macs-check.editionNote: The rule exists because a key's cuts are angled flats, and two adjacent cuts at very different depths have their slopes intersect below the top of the blade. The metal that should sit between them is not there, so the cutter either breaks through or leaves a fragile ridge that fails in service, usually inside a cylinder, which is the expensive way to find out. A violation is also a system design problem rather than only a cutting one. In a master key system the progression generates bittings automatically, and a progression that does not respect the rule will produce uncuttable change keys somewhere in the sequence, so checking the whole bitting list before any cylinder is pinned is the discipline, and the correction is made in the list rather than by whoever is standing at the machine. Two related checks travel with it and are reported alongside: a long run of identical depths produces a key that is easy to decode and to impression, and the shallowest cut at the shoulder position leaves the key weakest where it is worked hardest. Neither is a MACS matter but both are looked at in the same moment. The rule value and the depth range are manufacturer and keyway specific, and a value used for the wrong keyway gives a confident wrong answer.

assumptions.name: The rule is about metal, not arithmetic
assumptions.value: adjacent slopes intersect below the blade top and there is nothing left between the cuts

assumptions.name: Validate the whole bitting list
assumptions.value: a progression that violates the rule produces uncuttable keys somewhere in the sequence

assumptions.name: The value is keyway specific
assumptions.value: a MACS used for the wrong keyway gives a confident wrong answer

bond-work-index-power.formula: W = 10 Wi (1/sqrt(P80) - 1/sqrt(F80)) kWh per short ton (F80, P80 in microns); power_kW = W x feed rate (short tons per hour); hp = kW / 0.7457; with an available power, the finest product is P80 = [(kW/tph)/(10 Wi) + 1/sqrt(F80)]^-2.
bond-work-index-power.edition: Bond's third theory of comminution (F. C. Bond, 'The Third Theory of Comminution,' Trans. AIME 193, 1952; 'Crushing and Grinding Calculations,' Allis-Chalmers, 1961), by name.
bond-work-index-power.freeAccess: A published empirical law; the work index (from a Bond lab test), the sizes, and the feed rate are the user's inputs.
bond-work-index-power.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bond-work-index-power.editionNote: Energy at the mill pinion for a wet overflow ball mill in closed circuit, the condition Bond's work index is defined for; Rowland's efficiency factors for dry grinding, open circuit, fineness, mill diameter, oversize feed, and reduction ratio adjust it and are not applied. Wi is in kWh per short ton, Bond's original unit. A screen; the mill vendor's sizing governs.

assumptions.name: Bond's law
assumptions.value: W = 10 Wi (1/sqrt(P80) - 1/sqrt(F80)), sizes in microns at 80% passing

assumptions.name: Work index unit
assumptions.value: kWh per short ton; Wi is the energy from infinite size to 80% passing 100 microns

assumptions.name: Efficiency factors
assumptions.value: Rowland EF1-EF8 not applied

motor-locked-rotor-kva.formula: kVA/hp = upper bound of the Table 430.7(B) code-letter band; locked_rotor_kva = hp x kVA/hp; LRA = kVA x 1000 / (sqrt(3) x V) three-phase, kVA x 1000 / V single-phase.
motor-locked-rotor-kva.edition: The NEC 2023 Table 430.7(B) locked-rotor indicating code letters, mapping the nameplate code letter to a locked-rotor kVA/hp band, by name; the motor nameplate and measured inrush govern.
motor-locked-rotor-kva.freeAccess: NEC is free to read at nfpa.org/freeaccess. Table 430.7(B) and the locked-rotor kVA/hp bands are in the published code; the LRA relation is first-principles.
motor-locked-rotor-kva.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
motor-locked-rotor-kva.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Band
assumptions.value: uses the upper end of each code-letter kVA/hp band for a conservative starting current

assumptions.name: Not the design letter
assumptions.value: the code letter is about starting kVA; the design letter (A/B/C/D) describes the torque-speed curve

assumptions.name: Rule of thumb
assumptions.value: '6x FLA' holds only for mid-range code letters; high-code motors draw 7-8x

concrete-strength-from-modulus.formula: f'c = (Ec / (wc^1.5 x 33))^2, the ACI 318-19 19.2.2.1(a) relation Ec = wc^1.5 x 33 x sqrt(f'c) solved for the compressive strength (90 <= wc <= 160 pcf).
concrete-strength-from-modulus.edition: The ACI 318-19 19.2.2.1 modulus of elasticity of concrete, solved for f'c, by name.
concrete-strength-from-modulus.freeAccess: ACI 318 is readable free through the ACI online reading room at concrete.org; the 19.2.2 modulus provisions are in the published code.
concrete-strength-from-modulus.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
concrete-strength-from-modulus.editionNote: The inverse of concrete-elastic-modulus: the equivalent in-place compressive strength implied by a measured or specified elastic modulus. Useful for backing out f'c from a resonance / sonic-modulus test or a specified stiffness. The relation is the code secant value for 90 <= wc <= 160 pcf; the in-place modulus scatters with aggregate stiffness and moisture, so this is an equivalent strength, not a cylinder-break value. A design aid, not a substitute for the structural engineer of record's stamped design.

assumptions.name: Equivalent strength
assumptions.value: an equivalent in-place f'c from a stiffness, not a cylinder-break value

assumptions.name: Design value
assumptions.value: the in-place modulus varies with aggregate and mix

pole-embedment-depth.formula: Nonconstrained (Eq. 18-1): d = 0.5 A (1 + sqrt(1 + 4.36 h/A)), A = 2.34 P/(S1 b), S1 at one-third the embedment (implicit in d, solved iteratively). Constrained (Eq. 18-2): d^2 = 4.25 P h/(S3 b), S3 at the full embedment. Isolated poles: 2x lateral bearing per 1806.3.4.
pole-embedment-depth.edition: The IBC Section 1807.3 embedded posts and poles design equations and the 1806.3.4 isolated-pole increase, by name; the formula pair dates to the legacy UBC and is unchanged across the 2018-2024 IBC editions.
pole-embedment-depth.freeAccess: The IBC is viewable free through the ICC public-access portal (codes.iccsafe.org) and public code-hosting mirrors; 1807.3 is in every adopted edition.
pole-embedment-depth.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pole-embedment-depth.editionNote: The embedment definition stops at 12 ft - a deeper pole is outside the formula and flagged, not extrapolated. S1/S3 come from the LOCAL code's lateral-bearing table or the geotech report, entered per foot of depth - no Table 1806.2 values are reproduced. The 2x isolated-pole increase applies only where 1/2 in of motion at grade is acceptable (flagpoles, signs, fences), never where the pole supports a building. Poles carrying masonry or concrete need bracing per 1807.3.1; wood posts need AWPA U1 UC4B treatment. Lateral load only - vertical capacity and hole volume are separate tiles. The adopted edition and the AHJ govern - a design aid, not the engineer of record.

assumptions.name: Implicit S1
assumptions.value: the nonconstrained equation evaluates the lateral bearing at one-third the (unknown) embedment, so the tile solves it by bisection and the fuzzer verifies the root by back-substitution

assumptions.name: Constrained restraint
assumptions.value: the closed-form case assumes a rigid floor or pavement restrains the pole at grade

assumptions.name: Isolated-pole increase
assumptions.value: 2x tabulated lateral bearing where 1/2 in of grade-level motion is acceptable

assumptions.name: No code table
assumptions.value: the psf-per-ft lateral-bearing rate is a user input from the adopted code or geotech report

shaft-alignment-reverse-dial.formula: movable-shaft position y_A = +TIR_A / 2, y_B = -TIR_B / 2; slope = (y_B - y_A) / the plane spacing; move at a foot = -(y_A + slope x the distance from plane A to that foot), measured in the same sense as the plane spacing (positive = raise / add shim).
shaft-alignment-reverse-dial.edition: The reverse-dial alignment relations as standard millwright practice, by name. Both readings are rim readings, so no face measurement is involved and axial float does not affect the result. Bracket sag must be measured and subtracted. The machine manufacturer's alignment specification and the plant's precision maintenance procedure govern.
shaft-alignment-reverse-dial.freeAccess: Similar-triangles arithmetic on two dial readings; no manufacturer table is reproduced.
shaft-alignment-reverse-dial.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
shaft-alignment-reverse-dial.editionNote: Reverse-dial beats rim-and-face on anything with axial float or a long span, because two rim readings at two planes a known distance apart fully describe the misalignment -- two points define a line -- without any face being square. That is why it is the method of choice on long and spacer couplings. Everything after is one line extrapolated to the feet, and the single largest source of error is the direction convention: the distance to a foot is measured in the SAME sense as the plane spacing, and a foot on the far side of plane A carries a negative distance. The two readings describe the movable shaft with OPPOSITE signs, because the plane-A indicator rides the movable shaft and the plane-B indicator reads it from the stationary one: position = +TIR_A / 2 at A and -TIR_B / 2 at B, and each foot moves by the NEGATIVE of the extrapolated position. Readings of -0.014 and +0.022 in ten inches apart put the movable shaft 7.0 and 11.0 mils low, a -0.40 mils/in slope, so the front foot is raised 9.4 mils and the rear 16.6 -- both the same direction. Rexnord 538-214 prints -.020 and +.010 over 10.5 in as add .004 front and .001 rear, which this reproduces. Until 2026-09-26 the tile carried both halves with the same sign and moved the feet by the position, reversing the correction. Feet moving in opposite directions is a real and different signature, and reading two positive numbers as opposite is how a crew makes an alignment worse.

assumptions.name: Direction convention governs the answer
assumptions.value: a foot behind plane A carries a negative distance

assumptions.name: Bracket sag is not corrected here
assumptions.value: and reverse-dial invites long brackets

assumptions.name: Vertical solve only
assumptions.value: the horizontal solve is the same arithmetic on the side readings, corrected by jacking

fermenter-glycol-load.formula: extract = (OG - FG points) x gal / 46; Q = extract x 280 Btu/lb; crash = gal x 8.4 x 0.96 x dT / hours; ambient = A x U x (cellar - beer), at the fermenting beer for the fermentation load and the crashed beer for the crash; gpm = load / (60 x 8.6 x 0.90 x glycol rise).
fermenter-glycol-load.edition: Heat of fermentation about 280 Btu per lb of extract. The chiller manufacturer's capacity at the actual glycol temperature governs.
fermenter-glycol-load.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
fermenter-glycol-load.editionNote: The adiabatic rise (20 to 40 degF observed) checks the heat figure. The crash, not fermentation, sizes the chiller. spec-v1784 states shell gain as area x U x (room - beer), then charged the fermenting tank the gain of a crashed one (70 - 34 degF) while its beer is at 68; the tile takes each period at its own beer temperature, giving a 1,395 Btu/h peak fermentation load where the spec said 2,125. The conclusion strengthens: the crash is 3.1 times the fermentation load (the spec said 1.9), and a plant sized on fermentation is 68% short (the spec said 48).

assumptions.name: Beer heat capacity
assumptions.value: 8.4 lb/gal x 0.96 Btu/lb-F (ASHRAE Refrigeration Handbook ch. 8 Eq. 8 gives about 0.97 for 3-5% solids; Briggs 2014 prints wort at 4.0 kJ/kg K = 0.955); chiller vendors (American Chillers, Brau Supply) size the crash on water, 8.33 x 1.0, about 3% higher, and quote heat of fermentation per degree Plato per barrel rather than per lb of extract
assumptions.source: American Chillers; Brau Supply glycol sizing guides

assumptions.name: Beer
assumptions.value: 8.4 lb/gal at 0.96 Btu/lb-degF (0.90 until 2026-10-03)
assumptions.source: ASHRAE 1998 Refrigeration Handbook ch. 8 Eq. 8; Briggs of Burton 2014

assumptions.name: Glycol
assumptions.value: 8.6 lb/gal at 0.90 Btu/lb-degF

pretreatment-bath-dragout.formula: dragout = rate per 1,000 sq ft x area processed; concentrate lost = dragout x bath concentration; bath turnover = bath volume / dragout; single-rinse flow = dragout x dilution ratio; N counterflow stages need flow = dragout x (dilution ratio)^(1/N).
pretreatment-bath-dragout.edition: Standard metal finishing mass balance and the counterflow rinse dilution relation. The dragout rate is ENTERED and must be measured for the actual parts, racks and drain practice.
pretreatment-bath-dragout.freeAccess: A mass balance and an Nth root.
pretreatment-bath-dragout.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pretreatment-bath-dragout.editionNote: THE POWER LAW IS THE RESULT: the required flow falls as the Nth ROOT of the dilution ratio, so on a 1,000:1 target the step from one rinse tank to two cuts the water by 96.8%, the step from two to three adds only 2.2 points more, and a fourth stage saves about a fifth as much again while costing a tank, floor space and another transfer. That is why lines are built with two or three rinses and almost never with five. The relation assumes IDEAL MIXING in each stage, complete carry-over between stages and steady state, and a real rinse falls short of all three, so these flows are a LOWER BOUND. And the cheapest gallon is the one never dragged out -- longer drain time, a rack that lets solution run off instead of cupping, drain boards and air knives cut the chemical loss, the rinse water and the effluent load at once, because all three are proportional to the same number.

assumptions.name: Dragout is measured, not predicted
assumptions.value: roughly 0.4 to 2 gal per 1,000 sq ft for well-drained flat work, up to 10 for cupped or threaded parts
assumptions.source: weighing racked parts wet and dry over the tank

assumptions.name: Ideal counterflow
assumptions.value: perfect mixing, complete carry-over, steady state

assumptions.name: Discharge limits are not evaluated
assumptions.value: the permit governs what may leave the site
assumptions.source: the local sewer authority and the effluent guidelines

split-phase-leg-balance.formula: per-leg rating = rated watts / 240 V (or the data sheet figure); L1 A = 240 V loads + 120 V loads on L1; L2 A = 240 V loads + 120 V loads on L2; neutral A = |120 V on L1 - 120 V on L2|; total W = 240 x 240 V amperes + 120 x all 120 V amperes; balanced leg A = 240 V loads + all 120 V loads / 2.
split-phase-leg-balance.edition: WINCO, Portable Generator Load Balancing Guide (L-1008), named as the method (a 240 V ampere loads both legs, a 120 V ampere loads one); NEC Articles 445 and 590 cited by number for generators and temporary installations; the generator manufacturer's per-leg rating named as governing.
split-phase-leg-balance.freeAccess: Addition on the user's own load currents against the generator's rating; no code table is reproduced.
split-phase-leg-balance.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
split-phase-leg-balance.editionNote: A 120/240 V generator is two 120 V sources sharing a neutral, and its rated wattage assumes both are loaded equally. A 240 V load draws the same current on both legs and none on the neutral; a 120 V load draws only on its own leg. So a generator well under its rated watts can still trip a leg breaker when the heavy 120 V loads share one side, and the fix is usually one or two plugs moved. Many manufacturers treat about 80% of the leg rating as the continuous limit. The same arithmetic applies to a spider box or temporary panel fed from a 120/240 V source. Loads are running amperes; motor starting against surge capacity, three-phase sources, conductor sizing, GFCI protection and grounding, and building connection through a transfer switch or interlock are separate checks.

assumptions.name: 240 V loads on both legs
assumptions.value: a 240 V ampere loads each leg equally and carries no neutral current

assumptions.name: Per-leg rating
assumptions.value: rated watts / 240 V unless the data sheet states a per-leg figure

assumptions.name: Running current only
assumptions.value: motor starting and surge are checked separately

mppt-controller-output-current.formula: output current = array STC watts / battery nominal volts; controller = next common rating at or above it (20, 30, 40, 45, 60, 80, 100 A; 100 A units in parallel above that) or the chosen rating; array ratio = array watts / (controllers x rating x battery volts), clipping above 1.0; output conductor minimum current = 1.25 x the controller's rated continuous output.
mppt-controller-output-current.edition: Array watts over NOMINAL battery volts, which reads a little HIGH against how manufacturers rate: the Morningstar ProStar MPPT data sheet (rev. 1/2016) puts 350 W on its 25 A unit at 12 V and 700 W at 24 V, about 14 V and 28 V per amp, the charging voltage -- so this method can pick one size larger, the safe direction. The same sheet notes input power may exceed the nominal rating because the controller limits its output; NEC 690.8 cited by number for conductors at 125% of continuous current, subsection to be verified against the adopted edition.
mppt-controller-output-current.freeAccess: A division on the user's array and battery figures and a list of common trade ratings; no manufacturer table or NEC ampacity table is reproduced.
mppt-controller-output-current.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
mppt-controller-output-current.editionNote: An MPPT controller converts the array's high-voltage, low-current power into the battery's low-voltage, high-current charge, so its size is an output-current rating, and the current is the array watts divided by the battery voltage. That is why battery voltage is the largest lever in a small off-grid system: going from 12 V to 48 V cuts the controller current, the cable, and the fuse to a quarter. Manufacturers permit an array larger than the nominal rating because the controller clips at its limit, and the ratio makes that choice explicit. The output conductor is sized on the controller's rated continuous output rather than the calculated current, because the controller can deliver its full rating whenever the array drives it. Input voltage against cold open-circuit voltage, source-circuit current, and PWM controllers are separate checks.

assumptions.name: Power in about equals power out
assumptions.value: output current = array STC watts / battery nominal voltage

assumptions.name: Clipping is by design
assumptions.value: an array above the controller's nominal power is permitted; the controller limits its output

assumptions.name: 125% of rated output
assumptions.value: the output conductor and overcurrent device are selected on the controller's rated continuous current

usr-vertical-shore-capacity.formula: L/D = shore height (in) / post least actual width (in); Fa = 480,000 psi / (L/D)^2, capped at Fc = 1,100 psi (cap governs below L/D 20.9); P = Fa x post area; shore capacity = posts x P x species factor (1.00 / 0.85 / 0.75); L/D over 25 flagged, over 50 refused; lateral bracing = 2% of vertical capacity, 10% where aftershocks are expected.
usr-vertical-shore-capacity.edition: USACE US&R Structures Specialist Field Operations Guide (2006), Structural Calculations -- Material Properties; USACE US&R Shoring Operations Guide, Ed. 5.0 (2021), vertical shore design loads (8,000 / 5,000 / 3,500 lb for 4x4 at 8 / 10 / 12 ft; 20,000 / 12,000 / 7,500 lb for 6x6 at 12 / 16 / 20 ft), L/D 25 limit, and species factors; DHS BIPS 08 (2011) lateral strength of 2% of vertical load, 10% desirable with aftershocks.
usr-vertical-shore-capacity.freeAccess: A closed-form expression and published factors; the SOG and BIPS 08 are free federal publications.
usr-vertical-shore-capacity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
usr-vertical-shore-capacity.editionNote: The US&R method is a field-reduced column design: one Euler-shaped expression capped at the compression strength parallel to grain, taken on the shore height so the header and sole are counted. It reproduces the guide's published 4x4 design loads within 3% and its 6x6 loads within 6% (the formula gives 21,182 lb against the printed 20,000 at 12 ft). The L/D of 25 is a warning limit: below it an overloaded post crushes at its ends and creaks, giving rescuers time to leave; above it the post can buckle suddenly. The guide's own headline figure, 8,000 lb for a 4x4 in an 8 ft shore, sits at L/D 27.4, past that line, and the tile shows the flag there. The FOG permits a stress increase for US&R shores that this method does not apply. This overlaps column-buckling-wood (NDS Cp method for one member) and is kept as the distinct US&R field procedure.

assumptions.name: Slenderness is taken on shore height
assumptions.value: sole to top of header, divided by the post's least actual width

assumptions.name: L/D 25 is the no-warning line
assumptions.value: past it a post may buckle before its ends visibly crush; 50 is the maximum

assumptions.name: Bracing is a fraction of capacity
assumptions.value: 2% of vertical capacity minimum, 10% where aftershocks are expected
